nodes.label: Bilingual by Design (brand principle)
nodes.rationale: Arabic and English users deserve equal quality by architecture, not by translation; RTL is a first-class interface direction, reconsidered rather than mirrored from LTR.

nodes.label: Ownership over Dependency / No Lock-In
nodes.rationale: Clients receive a real codebase, documentation, and full ownership to avoid vendor dependency and plugin fragility.

nodes.label: Performance Is Product Quality
nodes.rationale: Speed affects trust, search visibility, and conversion, so performance is part of the build from day one (target < 1s TTI), not a late optimization task.

nodes.label: Site verification / IndexNow key file (hex token)
nodes.norm_label: site verification / indexnow key file (hex token)

nodes.label: BrandImage drop-in slot system
nodes.rationale: Named slots (hero, about, process, proof, aisa, loadingMark, notFound) map files to sections; BrandImage renders nothing until a file exists so a missing asset never breaks layout. Renders styled as one seed-locked system: near-black charcoal, single electric-blue accent, exported at 2x for clean Next.js downscaling.

nodes.label: Dynamic OG image over static og-image.png
nodes.rationale: The OG/social image is intentionally excluded from the brand drop-in folder because it is generated dynamically at app/[locale]/opengraph-image.tsx (1200x630), preferred over a static og-image.png.
nodes.norm_label: dynamic og image over static og-image.png

nodes.label: Velocity vs speed distinction
nodes.rationale: Speed is how fast the first feature ships; velocity is average delivery pace over 12 months. Bad agencies show high initial speed that collapses as technical debt compounds; good partners start slower but never decelerate.
nodes.author: Altruvex Team

nodes.label: Value-based milestone pricing model
nodes.rationale: Priced on delivered value in independently valuable phases rather than fixed price (rigid, corners cut) or time-and-materials (no efficiency incentive); client can pause after any phase.
nodes.author: Altruvex Team

nodes.label: Translation Theater anti-pattern
nodes.rationale: Translating text and adding dir=rtl is not localization; Arabic has different visual weight, scanning patterns, and technical requirements, so mirroring an English site produces a broken Arabic experience.
nodes.author: Altruvex Team

nodes.label: Translation tables database schema
nodes.rationale: Normalized per-language translation tables chosen over JSON columns because JSON cannot index efficiently, cannot enforce per-language content presence, and breaks relational integrity; translation tables allow adding a third language with no schema change and native indexed search.
nodes.author: Altruvex Team

nodes.label: Subdirectory URL locale strategy (/ar)
nodes.rationale: Subdirectory chosen over subdomain (splits domain authority, separate SSL, treated as separate site) and query parameter (weak SEO signals, poor caching); subdirectory consolidates authority and enables clean hreflang.
nodes.author: Altruvex Team

nodes.label: Audit-first rebuild sequencing (decision readiness)
nodes.rationale: Rebuilds fail when teams rebuild symptoms instead of causes; an audit separates trust, SEO, performance, workflow, and architecture problems, identifies what is salvageable, surfaces constraints, and produces decision readiness before scoping.

nodes.author: Altruvex Team

nodes.label: Compound interest of technical debt
nodes.rationale: Technical debt compounds unpredictably: the interest rate rises as the system evolves, debt begets more debt culturally, and every feature built on flawed foundations inherits the debt; quality code has an inverted interest rate and compounds as an asset.
nodes.author: Altruvex Team

nodes.label: Technical bankruptcy (100% capacity on debt service)
nodes.author: Altruvex Team
nodes.norm_label: technical bankruptcy (100% capacity on debt service)

nodes.label: Dependency debt (libraries as permanent liabilities)
nodes.rationale: Every dependency is owed maintenance forever (leftpad incident cited); Altruvex writes functionality in-house when it fits under ~200 lines and only takes dependencies for genuinely complex, actively maintained, security-vetted problems.
nodes.author: Altruvex Team

nodes.label: Article (EN): Why We Don't Use WordPress
nodes.author: Altruvex Team
nodes.norm_label: article (en): why we don't use wordpress

nodes.label: Plugin architecture fallacy
nodes.rationale: WordPress's 'plugin for everything' model makes black-box dependencies the foundation rather than a liability; a 30-plugin site is a Jenga tower with conflicting dependencies, update cascades, and abandoned code.
nodes.author: Altruvex Team

nodes.label: EAV performance tax (wp_postmeta)
nodes.rationale: WordPress's EAV metadata model trades flexibility for exponential query degradation at scale (800ms-2s multi-JOIN filters) versus 5-20ms on a normalized indexed PostgreSQL schema.
nodes.author: Altruvex Team

nodes.label: Fear of Update pattern
nodes.rationale: WordPress update cascades break themes and plugins, so owners stop updating to preserve stability, which is exactly when they become vulnerable to widely-published exploits.
nodes.author: Altruvex Team

nodes.label: Altruvex Design System & Brand Reference (design.md)
nodes.rationale: The token layer: single source of truth for what Altruvex looks/sounds like; every value pulled from the live codebase (apps/www), never invented. If a token disagrees with app/globals.css, the CSS wins.

nodes.label: Altruvex Brand & Positioning
nodes.rationale: Precision web engineering firm in Cairo, anti-template, founder-direct; proof model is 'this site itself is the proof' — the website demonstrates the production standard delivered to clients.

nodes.label: "X — not Y" Copy Idiom
nodes.rationale: Signature rhetorical move: state the standard, then dismiss the cheap alternative. Rule for social: every claim should be able to finish '…not ___' — if it can't name the lazy alternative it rejects, it's not on-brand.

nodes.label: Brand Blue Token (--brand #0E70F1)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately a single deep confident blue, not generic-SaaS blue; darkened to 48% L so white-on-brand passes WCAG AA (4.66:1). Fill/focus color, not a text color; the wordmark never uses it.

nodes.label: Neutral Ramp (--n-0 … --n-8)
nodes.rationale: The backbone: the site is mostly black-and-white (90% of every screen greyscale); color is an event, not a surface. Pure 0%-saturation neutrals are the engineered-neutral brand look.

nodes.label: Section Color Worlds (blue / orange / green)
nodes.rationale: Sections scoped to a local accent via --local-accent so the site stays mostly-mono while each section gets a quiet identity. Blue = brand/trust, orange = action/CTA/pricing, green = proof/shipped. One world per section; all AA-audited both modes.

nodes.label: Gradient Accent Palette
nodes.rationale: Display-only headline color (bg-clip-text), never body text. Gradient must match the section's color world, not contrast it. Rarity budget: ≤2 gradient accents per page, one per social graphic — a spotlight, not a theme.

nodes.label: Semantic State Colors (success/warning/error)
nodes.rationale: Off-limits for emphasis or branding: green means 'succeeded', not 'nice'. Approving color comes from the green world, never --success.

nodes.label: Type Scale & Font System (Outfit/Inter/Geist Mono/Vazirmatn)
nodes.rationale: Four typefaces with strict jobs. Two adjudicated deviations from the law layer: body leading 1.75 EN / 1.9 AR (above T5's band — airy premium voice on short marketing paragraphs) and display leading 1.0–1.08 (Latin display convention; Arabic headings never inherit it). Arabic letter-spacing forced to 0.

nodes.label: Eyebrow (Monospace Kicker)
nodes.rationale: Mono, uppercase, wide-tracked kicker reads as 'engineering / spec sheet' — the cheapest way to make an asset instantly look like Altruvex. Arabic drops the uppercase transform and tracking.

nodes.label: Emphasis System (Highlight / Accent / Strong / Dim)
nodes.rationale: The brand's typographic signature. Decision rule: calm/precision/quality/risk → Highlight (serif-italic); bold/value/conversion → Accent (gradient); loss-framed phrases stay Highlight even if conversion-y — coloring a warning is tonally wrong. ≤1 emphasis idea per paragraph; color and serif-italic are headline-only.

nodes.label: Motion System (GSAP 3 + Lenis)
nodes.rationale: Purposeful and quick — reveals, not decoration; not Framer Motion. Word-split rise+stagger headline reveal is the signature. Interaction hooks (magnetic, tilt) are desktop-fine-pointer-only flourishes gated on reduced-motion, pointer capability, and constrained devices.

nodes.label: 12px Button Radius Decision
nodes.rationale: Mid-radius voice adopted in the Apple design pass: not pill (consumer-friendly softness would undercut precision positioning), not sharp-corner brutalism (fights the refined Apple-adjacent surface language). 12px on a 40px control reads machined, not bouncy; nested elements follow inner = outer − padding.

nodes.label: Two-Layer Elevation System (4 levels)
nodes.rationale: Edges define depth first; each level is a tight contact layer whose opacity decays as elevation rises plus a soft key layer that grows with height. Four levels suffice — flat-with-a-whisper, not heavy material drop-shadows.

nodes.label: Liquid Glass Surfaces
nodes.rationale: Frosted, blurred, saturated panels for nav and overlays; degrades gracefully when the user prefers reduced transparency.

nodes.label: Underline Form Inputs
nodes.rationale: Underline, not box — a deliberate recognizable choice: a form reads as a stack of typographic lines rather than a grid of boxes. The box style reads as generic SaaS and breaks the brand.

nodes.label: Lucide Iconography
nodes.rationale: Lucide exclusively: thin-stroke, geometric, no fill, no duotone — pairs with the geometric type system and the 'engineering, not decoration' voice. Strictly functional markers, never decorative filler.

nodes.label: No-Photography Imagery Direction
nodes.rationale: The product uses no photography/illustration as a design element — type, tokens, geometric overlays, grain. A photo-led post is the fastest way to look like a generic agency, the brand's named enemy. Real screenshots of shipped work are the one legitimate imagery (proof, green world).

nodes.label: SectionHeading Composition Pattern
nodes.rationale: Canonical section header composes Eyebrow + h2 + optional emphasized clause + description. Passing accent=<gradient> renders <Accent> (value/conversion); omitting it renders <Highlight> (craft/restraint) — the §5 emphasis decision encoded in a single prop.

nodes.label: Social Media Translation Recipe
nodes.rationale: Five-part layout skeleton (eyebrow → headline → emphasis → body → wordmark footer), one color world, one emphasis per graphic. Litmus test: could a competitor swap their logo onto this post and have it still work? If yes, too generic.

nodes.label: Problem-Section Ember-on-Blue Mismatch
nodes.rationale: Tech-debt flag: problem-section inherits the blue world but applies an ember (orange) gradient on its heading — violates the gradient-must-match-the-world rule. Either intentional problem→action framing or a stray; open Phase 4/5 decision.

nodes.label: Altruvex Design Principles (Law Layer)
nodes.rationale: The codified perception/typography/color/spacing knowledge base the site is audited against — why, and what must hold. Numbers are heuristics, not citations. Every rule declares a script scope (latin-only rules never applied to Arabic); conflicts with the token layer are adjudicated in a change table, never silently.

nodes.label: T1 — Weight Hierarchy Needs Real Distance
nodes.rationale: Build weight hierarchy from steps of ≥200; a 100-unit gap is invisible at body sizes in most variable fonts. Hard-rule.
nodes.norm_label: t1 — weight hierarchy needs real distance

nodes.label: T3 — Non-Linear Modular Scale
nodes.rationale: Derive the type scale from a ratio (Major Third ×1.25 anchored at 16px), not taste-picked sizes; fluid clamps fine if endpoints sit on the scale.

nodes.label: T5 — Line Height by Role
nodes.rationale: Reading text loose (Latin 1.5–1.6), display tight (1.1–1.25). Arabic-variant: body 1.8–2.0, headings 1.25–1.35 — never copy Latin leading to Arabic.

nodes.label: T6 — Line Length (Measure)
nodes.rationale: Cap reading text: Latin 50–75 CPL, sweet spot ~66, hard ceiling 80 — long lines cause return-sweep errors. Arabic verified by words-per-line (~8–12) in Vazirmatn. Hard-rule.

nodes.label: T8 — All-Caps Is a Label Treatment
nodes.rationale: Caps only for short labels (≤3–4 words); running caps erase word-shape landmarks. Latin-only — Arabic has no case; the eyebrow drops transform and tracking in RTL.
nodes.norm_label: t8 — all-caps is a label treatment

nodes.label: T9 — Tracking Inverts Across the Display Threshold
nodes.rationale: Small text tracks slightly open, display slightly tight. Latin-only: connected Arabic script must have letter-spacing: 0 at every size (enforced !important in globals.css).
nodes.norm_label: t9 — tracking inverts across the display threshold

nodes.label: T12 — Typeface Signal Matches the Claim
nodes.rationale: Letterform genre chosen by the message: Outfit = clarity/confidence, Inter = neutral reading, Geist Mono = engineering signal, serif italic (Highlight) = craft/restraint. Arabic falls back to weight contrast — Arabic italics are not a real convention.
nodes.norm_label: t12 — typeface signal matches the claim

nodes.label: C2 — HSL Lightness Is Not Luminance
nodes.rationale: Never reason about contrast from HSL channel values; perception follows CIELAB-like curves. Verify by measured WCAG contrast, not channel math. Hard-rule.
nodes.norm_label: c2 — hsl lightness is not luminance

nodes.label: C4 — Structure Must Survive Greyscale
nodes.rationale: Build hierarchy in greyscale first; color may reinforce rank, never create it. The site's mostly-mono doctrine is this rule. Hard-rule.

nodes.label: C8 — Dark Mode Drops Chroma, Lifts Tone
nodes.rationale: Dark backgrounds amplify perceived saturation: derive dark variants by keeping hue, reducing chroma ~20–30%, lifting tone; verify contrast after. Heuristic — adapted in the reconciliation to a chroma cap.
nodes.norm_label: c8 — dark mode drops chroma, lifts tone

nodes.label: C9 — Token Architecture: Primitive → Semantic → System
nodes.rationale: Every color routed through the three-layer token chain; components never touch primitives or raw hex. Verified by grepping components for color literals (must be zero). Hard-rule.
nodes.norm_label: c9 — token architecture: primitive → semantic → system

nodes.label: C10 — Functional Hue Semantics Drive Assignment
nodes.rationale: Blue = trust/authority, warm high-chroma = action/urgency, green = positive/confirmation; site mapping blue world = brand/trust, orange = action/CTA/pricing, green = proof/shipped. Cultural context verified for the Arab-market audience.
nodes.norm_label: c10 — functional hue semantics drive assignment

nodes.label: C11 — Semantic Colors Signal State, Never Decorate
nodes.rationale: Success/warning/error tokens only for genuine state; approving color for emphasis comes from the color world, not --success. Hard-rule.
nodes.norm_label: c11 — semantic colors signal state, never decorate

nodes.label: C12 — Contrast Floors and the AAA Target
nodes.rationale: AA everywhere (body ≥4.5:1, large text/UI ≥3:1), design toward AAA (7:1) where the aesthetic allows; all scenes including inverted and tinted bands. Hard-rule.
nodes.norm_label: c12 — contrast floors and the aaa target

nodes.label: CI1 — Minimum Target Size 44px
nodes.rationale: Every interactive element gets a ≥44px effective hit target — tap errors are target-size errors (Fitts); a smaller visual can carry a larger hit area. Hard-rule; adapted to coarse pointers only in the reconciliation.

nodes.label: CI6 — Form Mechanics
nodes.rationale: Single column of grouped labeled fields, real-time inline validation at the field on blur/submit, progress indication on multi-step flows. Hard-rule.

nodes.label: CI8 — Radius Is a System and a Voice
nodes.rationale: All radii derive from one base; nested radii shrink (inner = outer − padding); the base is a deliberate brand-voice choice — very low reads precision/authority, large reads consumer-friendly. Hard-rule (nesting math) + judgment (voice).
nodes.norm_label: ci8 — radius is a system and a voice

nodes.label: CI9 — Elevation: Edges First, Two-Layer Shadows, Few Levels
nodes.rationale: Depth defined by edges first, confirmed by a two-layer shadow: soft directional key grows with height, tight ambient contact decays as elevation rises; ~5 levels suffice.
nodes.norm_label: ci9 — elevation: edges first, two-layer shadows, few levels

nodes.label: CI10 — Glass Has Five Parameters
nodes.rationale: Glass surfaces specified along light, refraction, depth, dispersion, frost — with a reduced-transparency fallback.

nodes.label: M2 — Anticipation Before Meaningful Reveals
nodes.rationale: Precede a meaningful reveal with a small counter-movement (~4–8% of travel, 15–20% of duration) so attention arrives before the motion; without it the reveal feels abrupt. Not for micro-hovers.

nodes.label: M3 — Motion Respects Capability and Preference
nodes.rationale: Gate all non-essential motion on prefers-reduced-motion, pointer capability, and constrained devices; the base interaction must work with motion off. Hard-rule.
nodes.norm_label: m3 — motion respects capability and preference

nodes.label: P8 — Jakob's Law: Innovate the Value, Not the Interface
nodes.rationale: Keep interface conventions users carry from the rest of the web; spend novelty on content and craft, not on relearning costs. Each deviation from convention needs a defended reason.
nodes.norm_label: p8 — jakob's law: innovate the value, not the interface

nodes.label: S2 — Columns: 12 / 8 / 4
nodes.rationale: 12-column desktop grid collapsing to 8 tablet / 4 mobile; grid type chosen by job. Deferred to a guidance heuristic for new sections in the reconciliation — retrofitting is a layout rewrite with no identified defect.

nodes.label: S8 — Icon Geometry
nodes.rationale: Consistent 24px bounding box, 2px trim, even 2px strokes on the pixel grid (Lucide default conforms); shape mass compensated; directional icons mirror in RTL.

nodes.label: Chromatic Intent × Design Principles — Phase 2 Reconciliation (July 2026)
nodes.rationale: The adjudication record reconciling the live token system against the law layer: every accepted change in a change table, every rejected principle with its reason. Notable rejections: 800-weight hero triad (display voice is deliberately light), strict 1.5–1.6 body leading (airy premium voice kept), warm-tinted greyscale (engineered 0%-S neutrality is the identity).
nodes.norm_label: chromatic intent × design principles — phase 2 reconciliation (july 2026)

nodes.label: Dark-Mode Chroma Cap (C8 Adapted)
nodes.rationale: Instead of C8's full −20–30% chroma cut, dark accents are capped at the light variant's OKLCH chroma — preserving audited dark vibrancy while killing amplification (the principle's actual mechanism). Orange trimmed from C 0.168→0.134, green from 0.146→0.100; contrast re-verified ≥6.6:1 on #121212.

nodes.label: Pointer-Coarse 44px Targets (CI1 Adapted)
nodes.rationale: 44px enforced where tap errors happen (coarse pointers, via pointer-coarse: variants); compact fine-pointer sizes kept — mouse precision doesn't need 44px and the compact sizes are part of the visual language.

nodes.label: OKLCH as Canonical Color-Reasoning Space
nodes.rationale: Every new/changed color token is decided and verified in OKLCH (perceptual chroma/lightness + measured WCAG contrast), then authored in HSL. Authored-format migration deferred — rewriting 100+ working tokens is churn with zero visual delta. Gives C2's law a named working space.

nodes.label: Gradient Key Tiering (Core / Reserve / Editorial)
nodes.rationale: No key deleted: core keys (iris/ember/forest/mint) are the only ones sections may use; reserve keys need a world match; editorial keys fenced to MDX <Mark> + the playground. neon/candy flagged for retirement if still unused at next audit.

nodes.label: Phase 3 — 2026 Trend Verification
nodes.rationale: Filter: relevant to Altruvex → passes through the existing language → strengthens 'precision engineering'; all three or it's out. Adopted OKLCH reasoning + DTCG tokens as export path; rejected dopamine palettes, neo-brutalism, neumorphism, kinetic type, experimental nav, 3D/WebGL (spectacle spends the sub-1s performance budget on decoration).
